lesson.title: React useEffect() Hook: Dependencies and Cleanup
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

goalMatch.note: This video covers exactly what you asked for: running effects on mount with an empty array, re-running them on state changes via dependencies, and cleanup through the return function.

sources.title: React useEffect() Hook: Dependencies and Cleanup

steps.title: Build a counter component
steps.instructions: Create a Vite React project (npm create vite@latest my-app -- --template react) and in src/MyComponent.jsx import useState and useEffect, add a count state starting at 0, a paragraph showing 'Count: {count}' and an Add button whose handler does setCount(c => c + 1). Render <MyComponent /> from App.jsx and run npm run dev.

targets.caption: Count state variable initialized to zero
Handler that increments count using the previous state
Rendered counter paragraph and Add button

explanations.topic: Importing useState and useEffect from React
Creating a count state variable with a setter
Updater function using the previous state of count

hints: Start by importing both hooks: import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react'.

Declare state with const [count, setCount] = useState(0); and show it in a

Count: {count}

.
Add <button onClick={addCount}>Add</button> and define function addCount() { setCount(c => c + 1); }.
Make sure App.jsx imports MyComponent and returns <MyComponent />, then run npm run dev.
common_mistakes: Writing onClick={addCount()} which calls the function during render instead of passing it.
Forgetting to export default MyComponent or to render <MyComponent /> in App.jsx.
Using useState() without 0, so the count shows blank or NaN after clicking.
Returning two sibling elements without wrapping them in a fragment <>...</>.
Importing useEffect from the wrong package or misspelling it (useEfect).

steps.title: Update title on every render
steps.instructions: Inside MyComponent call useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }) with no dependency array so the title updates on every render. Try adding [] as the second argument to see it run only on mount, then revert.

targets.caption: Call useEffect inside your component
Set the document title from the count state

explanations.topic: useEffect runs side code every time the component re-renders
useEffect takes two arguments: a function and an array of dependencies
Omitting the dependency array runs the effect after every render, including mount
An empty dependency array runs the effect only once on mount
One-and-done effects like a static title should use an empty array

hints: Import useEffect alongside useState from 'react', then call it near the top of your component body.
Pass useEffect an arrow function and leave off the second argument so it runs on every re-render.
Inside the arrow function, assign document.title a template string that includes ${count}.
To see mount-only behavior, add [] as the second argument, click Add, notice the title stops updating, then remove the [] again.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react', causing 'useEffect is not defined'.
Using regular quotes instead of backticks, so the title literally shows ${count}.
Leaving the empty [] dependency array in place after the experiment, so the title never updates past the first render.
Placing useEffect inside a handler or after the return statement instead of at the top level of the component.
Calling useEffect(document.title = ...) without wrapping the code in a function.

steps.title: Depend on count and add Subtract
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx pass [count] as the useEffect dependency array. Add a Subtract button calling subtractCount, which does setCount(c => c - 1).

targets.caption: count added to the dependency array
new subtractCount function
Subtract button on the page

explanations.topic: Putting a value in the dependency array: the effect runs on mount and whenever that value changes
With no dependency array the effect runs on every re-render, even for unrelated reasons
Whether count goes up or down, the change triggers the effect and the title updates

hints: The second argument to useEffect is an array. Which state value should the effect watch?
Write the array as [count] after the arrow function, separated by a comma.
Copy your add function, rename it subtractCount, and change the updater to c => c - 1.
Add <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button> next to the Add button.
common_mistakes: Leaving the dependency array empty ([]), so the title only updates on mount
Writing onClick={subtractCount()}, which calls the function during render
Using setCount(count - 1) instead of the updater form c => c - 1
Keeping the copied function name, which defines addCount twice

steps.title: Add color state as dependency
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx add color state ('green'), a Change color button whose changeColor toggles green/red, and style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}. Include color in the title and use [count, color] as dependencies.

targets.caption: Toggle color between green and red
Both values in the dependency array
New button below Subtract

explanations.topic: Updater function with ternary to flip state
Style attribute needs a JavaScript object (double curly braces)
Title doesn't update on color change when color is missing from deps
Effect reruns when any dependency changes

hints: Create a second state variable for color with useState, starting at 'green'.
changeColor should call setColor with an updater: c => c === 'green' ? 'red' : 'green'.
Style the count paragraph with style={{color: color}}. The outer braces embed JavaScript, the inner braces make the object.
Use color in the document.title template and list it in the dependency array: [count, color].
common_mistakes: Using single braces style={color: color}, which is a syntax error, or passing a string style.
Adding color to the title but forgetting the dependency array, so the title only updates when count changes.
Writing onClick={changeColor()}, which calls the function during render.
Comparing with = instead of === in the ternary.

Forgetting the
so the button sits inline (cosmetic only).

steps.title: Track window width and height
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, create width and height state initialized to window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight, render 'Window width: {width}px' and 'Window height: {height}px', and write handleResize to set both. Add window.addEventListener('resize', handleResize) with a console.log in the component body to watch listeners pile up.

targets.caption: Width and height state initialized from the window
handleResize updates both state variables
Resize listener added in the component body (no useEffect yet)
Rendered width and height update while resizing

explanations.topic: Initializing state from window.innerWidth / innerHeight
Nothing updates on resize without an event listener
Adding a resize listener in the component body
Every re-render adds another listener, so they pile up

hints: Create two state variables with useState, using window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight as their initial values.

Render two

elements: 'Window width: {width}px' and 'Window height: {height}px'.
Write a handleResize function that calls setWidth(window.innerWidth) and setHeight(window.innerHeight).
In the component body, call window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) and console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"). Resize the window and watch the console count climb.
common_mistakes: Calling handleResize() when adding the listener: addEventListener("resize", handleResize()) instead of passing the function itself.
Lowercase setter typo, e.g. 'setheight' instead of 'setHeight' (the presenter fixes this at 13:12).
Using window.outerWidth or screen.width instead of window.innerWidth.
Forgetting to import useState from 'react'.
Wrapping the listener in useEffect already. This step intentionally puts it in the component body to show listeners piling up.

steps.title: Add listener once on mount
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, move the addEventListener call and console.log into useEffect(() => { ... }, []) so the listener is added only on mount.

targets.caption: Wrap the listener setup in useEffect
Empty array = run only on mount
Log appears once (twice in Strict Mode) after resizing

explanations.topic: Adding a listener every render piles up thousands of listeners; add it once on mount
useEffect takes a function and a dependency array
Empty dependency array runs the effect only on mount
Strict Mode runs effects twice in development (setup, cleanup, setup)

hints: Don't call addEventListener directly in the component body; it runs on every render.
Move the addEventListener and console.log lines inside useEffect(() => { ... }).
Pass an empty array [] as the second argument to useEffect so it runs only on mount.
Open DevTools Console and resize the window: the log should show once (or twice under Strict Mode), not on every resize.
common_mistakes: Leaving the dependency array off entirely, so the effect still runs after every render.
Putting [width, height] in the array, which re-adds the listener on every resize.
Forgetting to import useEffect from 'react'.
Thinking the doubled console log is a bug — it's React Strict Mode in development.
Calling handleResize() instead of passing handleResize to addEventListener.

steps.title: Return a cleanup function
steps.instructions: Inside that useEffect in src/MyComponent.jsx, return a function that calls window.removeEventListener('resize', handleResize) and logs a removal message. In StrictMode the console shows setup, cleanup, then setup once more.

targets.caption: The cleanup function returned from useEffect removes the resize listener
In StrictMode the console shows added, removed, then added once more

explanations.topic: Returning a function from useEffect performs cleanup
Cleanup runs before the next re-render or when the component unmounts
Remove event listeners on unmount to avoid unexpected behavior
StrictMode runs the effect, cleans it up, then runs it again in development

hints: Cleanup goes inside the same useEffect that adds the listener: return a function at the end of the effect body.
Write `return () => { ... }` inside the effect, after the addEventListener call.
Inside the returned function, call window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize) and console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED").
Refresh the page and open DevTools > Console. You should see ADDED, REMOVED, ADDED because of StrictMode.
common_mistakes: Calling removeEventListener directly in the effect body instead of inside a returned function.
Passing a new inline arrow function to removeEventListener instead of the same handleResize reference.
Misspelling the event name, for example 'resized' instead of 'resize', so the listener is never removed.
Writing `return removeEventListener(...)`, which runs it immediately instead of returning a function.
Expecting REMOVED to log on every resize. It only logs on the StrictMode remount or on unmount.

steps.title: Add a second useEffect hook
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx, add another useEffect that sets document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}` with dependency array [width, height]. Resize the browser window and watch the tab title update.

targets.caption: Add a second useEffect that writes the width and height into the page title
Run this effect only when width or height changes
Resize the window and watch the tab title update

explanations.topic: A component can have more than one useEffect hook
The effect should run when width or height changes
The effect runs on mount, then again whenever a dependency changes

hints: Under your first useEffect, add another useEffect(() => { ... }) call. A component can have several.
Inside it, assign a template string to document.title: `Size: ${width} x ${height}`.
Pass [width, height] as the second argument so the effect re-runs only when those values change.
Save the file, then drag the browser window's edge and check the tab title.
common_mistakes: Using quotes instead of backticks, so ${width} shows up literally in the title
Leaving out the dependency array, which makes the effect run after every render
Using an empty [] dependency array, so the title never updates on resize
Placing the second useEffect inside the first effect or inside the cleanup function instead of at the component's top level
Forgetting that the earlier color/count effect also sets document.title, so the two effects overwrite each other
